messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: Dedicated pool saturation detected in us-west-2. p99 latency > 6s for streaming endpoints, queue depth > 1500. Severity: P1. @oncall-eng on call.

maya: acked. seeing alerts too — investigating. first glance: streaming stalls + handshake timeouts. tagging runtime and platform.

liam: attaching quick metrics snapshot from internal dashboard: 
- global p95: 1.45s (baseline ~0.12s)
- global p99: 6.2s (baseline ~0.35s)
- streaming stall rate: 4.9% of streams hitting stall state (normally <0.2%)
- dedicated us-west-2 queue depth: 1,730 requests
- warmup success rate last 10m: 62% (handshake timeouts rising)

sarah: anyone see autoscaler churn? could be slow warmup + handshake deadlocks.

liam: yes — autoscaler logs show warmup tasks queued and repeated handshake timeouts to warmup workers. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] autoscaler: pool=ded-usw2-1 warmup_task_enqueue id=wk-129 attempts=3
[2026-03-15T10:12:06Z] handshake: worker=wk-129 status=timeout duration=30s
[2026-03-15T10:12:09Z] autoscaler: warmup_failed id=wk-129 reason=handshake_timeout
```

and backend is reporting high memory pressure on a subset of instances which slows kernel selection and kv-cache loading.

devon: customer impact data from support: AcmePay (high throughput) saw ~7% request errors and many streams truncated; several enterprise customers reported slow UI refresh. CS ticket numbers: #CS-2219, #CS-2223.

cs-sam: flagged to Account execs. they want ETA and mitigation steps.

oncall-eng: i'm going to try a quick mitigation: temporarily divert low-priority traffic to hosted fallback model variant and enable small-batch mode for streaming on the affected pool. this should reduce queue pressure and kv rehydration overhead.

andrew: steps I can run now: 
1) reduce batch target for pool ded-usw2-1 
```
rictl pool update --pool ded-usw2-1 --batch-target 4
```
2) manual warmup of 6 extra workers in pool (temp) 
```
rictl pool warmup --pool ded-usw2-1 --instances 6 --mode keepalive
```
3) set handshake timeout longer to tolerate slow init for 10m 
```
rictl config set autoscaler.handshake_timeout 45s --scope pool:ded-usw2-1
```
I can run 1+2 now if we want.

maya: do it. devon please prepare a traffic-routing rule to divert 20% of lower-tier traffic to hosted fallback. cs-sam, tell AcmePay we have mitigations in place and we're reducing background pressure; will follow up in 15m with metrics.

devon: making routing change now — creating a temporary route: 
```
router.apply --region us-west-2 --rule "if customer_tier == low then route->hosted-fallback" --weight 20%
```

ops-bot: NOTE: routing change applied at 2026-03-15T10:24:11Z by devon.

liam: after batch reduction + routing 20% offloaded, seeing initial improvement: queue depth down to ~900, p95 to 0.9s, p99 to 3.1s. still above SLO but trending down. streaming stalls down to 1.8%.

maya: good. still need to stop handshake timeouts. andrew, did warmup succeed?

andrew: manual warmup finished for 6 instances, 5/6 succeeded; 1 worker failed health check (oom on startup). autoscaler log shows some workers failing due to resource pressure on host. we should avoid scheduling more on those hosts.

liam: identified a noisy host group (host-mix-12) with elevated memory churn. marking them drained for new warmups. 
```
rictl host drain --host-group host-mix-12 --reason "elevated-memory-churn"
```

devon: rebalanced warmups to other hosts — warmup success now 92% last 5m. p99 at 2.1s, streaming stalls 0.6%. queue depth ~420.

cs-sam: AcmePay responded: they see significant improvement but still have occasional 5s spikes. asked for postmortem and RCA. I've promised a 2hr update.

maya: we should open a paging to Platform SRE to investigate root cause of host memory churn + why autoscaler couldn't spin up warmups faster. moving to Platform channel for follow-up. tagging @liam and @andrew for initial triage.

liam: quick hypothesis: a model quantization kernel regression caused slower init times & memory footprint increase on a recent runtime roll (deploy 2026-03-15T09:50). I'll check rollout history.

andrew: rollout logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:50:12Z] runtime-deploy: version=v2.14.3 -> v2.15.0 target=dedicated-runtime
[2026-03-15T09:50:30Z] canary: 5 nodes -> success
[2026-03-15T09:50:55Z] rollout: 80% nodes updated
[2026-03-15T10:05:00Z] rollout: 100% updated
```
We might correlate that with the start of warmup failures.

maya: okay escalate. immediate mitigations implemented: routing offload, batch reduction, manual warmup, host drains. customer impact reduced but not zero.

oncall-eng: handing off to next on-call in 30m — leaving action list: 
- Platform SRE to investigate runtime v2.15.0 memory/regression
- Autoscaler team to review handshake timeout logic and in-flight warmup queue handling
- Product/CS to coordinate customer follow-ups and compensations if needed

devon: adding runbook note: temporary playbook entry to prefer warmer hosts and extend handshake timeout during mass warmups.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll update the incident channel and our pagerduty incident with current mitigations and timeline. next update in 15m or earlier if regressions.

liam: uploading brief logs to incident ticket: /internal/incidents/INC-2026-3340/logs.tar.gz

cs-sam: noted. i'll follow up with AcmePay and the other affected customers.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-3340 created and assigned to Platform SRE. priority=P1.

maya: handing off fully to @liam (Platform/Runtime lead) at 3340014800 for continued triage. leaving channel.

liam: ack — will coordinate root cause and postmortem.

oncall-eng: closing active paging loop in this thread; if anything spikes again re-paging Platform SRE and Eng Runtime.

maya: thanks all :thumbsup:
